quote: Are you So sorry. Are you logged in to the app right now?
stewart_read: Customer had already given a workable ballpark ('60 to a 100... but summer months were even higher') from her own spreadsheet. Instead of using that number to anchor the conversation, the rep pushed her into the utility app, starting a seven-minute detour.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have needed the more precise kWh graph because this appears to be a paid lead requiring the bill before booking per context.lead_types_and_bill_collection_rules — but lead_type is not stated anywhere in this transcript, so that requirement cannot be confirmed either way.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to accept a customer-stated ballpark as sufficient to move the call forward when digging for exact figures visibly stalls the conversation; verify lead_type before insisting on a precise bill screenshot.

quote: I'm not seeing a yearly kilowatt hours.
stewart_read: This is the point where bill_collection's own alternative-path guidance calls for a pivot to verbal read-back within about two minutes of friction. The rep is already past that window and continues coaching the customer through app navigation instead.
alternative_hypothesis: It's possible the rep judged the app path faster than a verbal read-back would be, but the eventual outcome (still not resolved by 09:00+) argues against that read — lead_type is unknown here too, so it's unclear whether a screenshot was even mandatory for this lead per context.lead_types_and_bill_collection_rules.
coaching_implication: Train a hard 2-minute clock: if the customer is visibly struggling with the utility site, switch to 'just read me the number off the page' rather than continuing to troubleshoot their app.

quote: Well, the last three months, it will be a month and a half of service. So that makes no sense
stewart_read: By this point the customer is pointing out the data itself is unreliable (she wasn't home for six months), yet the rep continues pursuing the same data-capture goal instead of stepping back and offering to defer bill collection to the specialist appointment.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is best supported here — there is no evidence the rep recognized the ask had become unproductive; the call continues to unravel over the next minute.
coaching_implication: When the customer volunteers that the data won't be representative, that's the cue to drop the bill ask entirely and pivot straight to scheduling.

quote: I have a a family emergency that came up, so this is kind of the lowest priority.
stewart_read: This is a direct vulnerability disclosure — a family emergency, one of the schema's named trigger categories. The rep's entire response is a flat 'Okay,' with no acknowledgment of the situation before continuing the call mechanics.
coaching_implication: Coach a specific human acknowledgment ('I'm sorry to hear that — let's not worry about this today') before moving to any next-step logistics. This single word response is the clearest missed trust-gift moment in the call.

stewart_read: The customer is asking a basic company-legitimacy question nearly eleven minutes into the call — a sign the intro never firmly established who Ion is or where they operate, leaving this gap to surface only as the customer is already exiting.
alternative_hypothesis: This may be ordinary end-of-call curiosity rather than a sign the intro failed, since the customer had already engaged for ten minutes before asking — but the schema's coaching_note that the intro should answer 'is this a scam?' up front suggests this question arriving this late is itself informative.
coaching_implication: Reinforce that intros.standard's legitimacy framing (company name + reason for call, ideally region/context) should preempt exactly this kind of question rather than leaving it to surface unprompted at the end.

quote: We're not really we don't have, like, a main headquarters. We just have teams everywhere.
stewart_read: The rep's answer about company structure is halting and self-contradicting (no headquarters, then immediately reversing to confirm one exists in Utah), which reads as unprepared rather than confident, at a moment when the customer is already reconsidering the relationship.
alternative_hypothesis: Reactive read is well-supported: the correction at 11:19 ('Or, actually, we do have a headquarters') shows the rep talking through uncertainty live rather than executing a deliberate strategy. This exchange follows the family-emergency disclosure and the customer's decision to pause, so it is better read as a rep stumbling on a tangential question than as the cause of her withdrawal.
coaching_implication: Have a clean, single-sentence answer ready for basic company questions (state HQ, region served) so uncertainty doesn't compound in a moment where the customer is already ambivalent.

quote: please take me off of all inquiry list, like, updates because I think you guys have been calling me all the time
stewart_read: This is an excessive-contact complaint, a pattern the schema notes is not yet script-defined (protocols section TBD item). The rep accepts the removal request without addressing or resolving the underlying frustration about call frequency.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer had already disclosed a family emergency and was actively disengaging, resolving the contact-frequency complaint on this call may not have been realistic — the priority was already exiting gracefully rather than repairing the relationship.
coaching_implication: Flag this call as a real-world example for Kenny's uncatalogued 'excessive_contact_complaint' protocol; the floor needs a defined response for when a customer says they've been over-contacted.
